name: assignment-brief
description: Author or assess a bounded agent assignment with required and stretch goals, evidence acceptance, concerns, confidence bars, finite budgets and pivot or stop rules using Assignment Kit. # Assignment brief

Read [the adoption guide](../../../docs/assignment-kit.md), then the canonical
[library contract](../../../kits/assignment-kit/README.md). For a changed domain
boundary, load the project's intent router and relevant decisions first.

Use existing project goal and plan IDs. Separate the requested outcome, explicit
requirements, assumptions and exclusions. Establish independently reviewed required
scope before using it to detect omissions. A model-generated list cannot attest its
own completeness. Use Catalog Kit's current stable-key/definition bindings where
available, without moving domain authority into the catalog.

Create typed Assignment/Scope/Input values under the consuming workflow's normal
owned files. Do not create another project intent file, ledger or status truth.
Start with one required goal/profile and finite budget/deadline; add stretch goals,
concerns and deterministic escalation/pivot/stop rules only for actual needs.
Reference versioned governing intent and policy. Specify eligible evidence methods,
source/subject/definition pins, freshness, explicit unknowns and applicable tests.
Never use raw model confidence as acceptance proof. Optional confidence readings
need the exact observation, independently qualified calibration basis and site.

Run the actual `assignmentkit.Evaluate` path with injected time and real retained
observations. A textual brief or this skill is guidance, not enforcement. Report
each required goal, unresolved concern, usage, matched rule and next disposition.
Invalid input, missing evidence, exhausted work and stopped attempts cannot become
success. Stretch outcomes cannot compensate for a required failure.

Keep result trust caller-declared and authority false. The application owns evidence
authenticity, permission, budget reservation, actual execution and the actual stop.
Changed requirements require a newly reviewed assignment/scope/policy snapshot.
Do not execute an escalation, contact someone, install a hook or widen permissions
because the evaluator recommends it. Preserve failed and partial receipts with the
consumer's access/retention controls, and reconcile its existing work order honestly.
